Salux is truly one of those "Where have you been all my life???" hidden products.

I purchased my first bundle of Salux cloths back in September 2016 and I have hardly felt so good about discovering a hidden or abstract product. The tag line on the packaging and on the official Salux website "A shower isn't a shower without Salux." sounds like some corny slogan, but it is something most will agree with after using the Salux cloth just for the first time. I prefer the "Super Hard" version of the Salux cloth for showers, but even the standard version here is great to lather and scrub the entire body. I now think: How the hell did I shower all these years with just a loofa? The Salux gets your arms, your upper and lower back, your underarms, your "Swimsuit Area" (Tee Hee :) your legs, everything. I have dealt with oily skin and acne, and the Salux cloth is also a game-changer for addressing those issues as well. Certain dry bar soaps like the line of Nubian Heritage soaps have always been more beneficial to my skin, and the Salux cloth's ability to lather up so well with a minor amount of soap has not only allowed me to apply these soaps all across my body (I get the occasional back zit) but it also allowed me to shave with those types of soaps. I have saved money on buying shaving creams and gels because the lather produced by the Salux cloth is so abundant that I coat my whole face in lather, which allows me to shave even easier than before. Dry soaps also last longer than liquid/gel cleansers, so you will also be saving money in that regard. Given the type of soap you use, you will even save money on shampoo since you can wash your hair with the abundant lather. Believe the hype, everybody! Unless you have super super sensitive skin, you will be a life-long patron of the Salux Japanese wash cloth. Just be wary of counterfeits out there; The official website saluxshop.com has an entire section devoted to identifying the fake Salux cloths out there.

It's obviously not a genuine mirror as a heavy glass mirror would not work. I run a hot shower and I don't see the mirror getting foggy with any consistency. I use a squeegee on my shower tile when I'm done and this has a low-enough profile that I can just lightly graze it while I'm squeegeeing the tile and not have much disruption. Update: after about a year, I couldn't clean the haze that built up on it. Because it adheres directly to the wall, you have to do some occasional cleaning to keep mold at bay. I found a superior option in the Shave Well Company Deluxe Anti-Fog Shower Mirror, which hangs on a tiny hook suction cup. Because it hangs on a hook, that mirror can be removed and run under the shower water, thereby washing away the fog and keeping the mirror clean. And, since only the single suction cup attaches to the wall rather than the entire mirror, that mirror doesn't risk getting moldy.

Painfully Bad! (Yes, actual pain!)

RETURNED! First of all, I am barefoot all day long, so I need to clean the bottoms of my feet, but I also do a lot of dying, and constantly have dye spraying or dripping on the tops of my feet as well. So when I get in the shower, I usually end up scrubbing my feet with a brush anyway - I thought this would be great, because it scrubs the bottoms *and* tops at the same time! Yay! What a great idea!.... NOT. Problems; 1. First problem, the suction cups suck (and not in the way they should!) The thing slides around, and is nearly impossible to keep still long enough to get on a good scrub. I spent more time chasing it around the shower with my foot, than it would ever have taken me to just scrub my feet by hand. Even when I was able to keep it still long enough to start scrubbing, every time I pushed my foot into it with enough pressure to actually scrub, it started to move again, and here I am chasing it around the shower again! So #1, bad suction. 2. And this is the worst part! When I was able to push it up against the side of the shower so it wouldn't slide around so much, I don't know if it's because I have high arches or what, but when I put my foot all the way in, that hard blue plastic across the top just scraped the tops of my feet raw! Very painful, and even feeling kind of bruised as well!! So even if it didn't slide around, and make it impossible to scrub for more than 5 seconds, it is so painful to put my foot all the way in, so I wasn't able to scrub the whole foot, I had to just do the bottom of my toes, and then going only up to about half of my foot, stopping once it got to the hard blue plastic on top. So after my first use, my feet remained dirty, and now have painful scratches on the tops of my feet. Not a pleasant experience to say the least!! I saw another one on here that only does the bottoms, so I am going to cross my fingers, and try that one, and hope that the suction cups work better! It won't get the tops at the same time, so it won't hurt them either!

but I did note that my mascara was going on better - making my lashes appear longer

I used this product for 8 weeks. The packaging indicated I would see a difference as early as 2 weeks, with its full effects seen in 6 weeks. At two weeks, I didn't 'see' a difference, but I did note that my mascara was going on better - making my lashes appear longer. This continued to be the case, even after 8 weeks of use: my eye lashes, without mascara, did not appear longer, but with the assistance of mascara and the serum, the lashes appeared a little longer at the outer edges of the eye (not the lashes of the inner eye). Note: the serum can only be used on the upper eyelid lashes, not on the lower lashes. Also, if too much serum is applied to the upper lid, it can seep into the eye and cause burning.
